upstream_provenance.source_context:
# Treat OH database selection as a storage contract with migration implications

## Platform difference

A database abstraction remaining in Dart does not remove its native SQLite dependency; replacing it with preferences/JSON also changes storage semantics.

## Implementation

Pica Comic introduces OH SQLite loading, a database abstraction and JSON-backed preferences. Bugaoshan initially selects a preferences/JSON database fallback on OH, then sets that selector to false after adopting the CPF sqflite implementation. Nexora uses bundled rusqlite with an app-support database. Zhiji retains Drift NativeDatabase and sqlite3_flutter_libs, but its earlier study did not establish a working OH native library path.

## Applicability

Review actual engine selection, data location, schema, transactions and old data compatibility, not just successful pub resolution. The Bugaoshan fallback is historical rather than its final recorded policy.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Do not claim SQLite is unavailable merely because one plugin is missing. Preferences can have different transaction/concurrency/durability behavior. Reverting a backend selector does not itself prove users' existing fallback data was migrated.

## Verification

Test create/read/update, restart, schema upgrades, concurrent writes, migration of existing data and failure recovery using the selected native library in a release app.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
